title: Birb Hangout
summary: A multiplayer 3D game and creative-engineering environment for expressive character interaction, spatial annotation, and repeatable visual review.
landingDeck: Birb Hangout combines game design, realtime multiplayer interaction, 3D annotation, and purpose-built harnesses for reviewing creative work.
landingHighlights: Designs character motion, seating, proximity, room objects, and media as one social interaction system.
Builds focused harnesses for animation, camera, interaction, and visual-reference review during creative development.
Uses 3D annotations and separate motion, interaction, multiplayer, and deployment checks to make review specific and repeatable.
problem: A shared 3D room needs to communicate presence, attention, mood, and activity through character behavior and spatial interaction.
approach: A Three.js client renders the lounge and characters, a Colyseus room server synchronizes shared state, and focused harnesses isolate creative tasks for review.
output: An actively developed React Three Fiber and Colyseus game with synchronized room state, diegetic social activities, consent-gated interactions, frame-level animation diagnostics, and world-space visual annotations.

methodology.evaluation: Animation Lab captures paired baseline/candidate frames and speed, acceleration, and jerk traces. Dream Studio and Rig Studio store annotated PNGs, strokes, comments, camera pose, and world position. Scripted checks cover interaction and multiplayer transitions.
methodology.boundary: Current evidence covers local and deployed interaction slices, multiplayer state checks, and visual review. Large-scale concurrency and cross-browser media validation remain open.

role: I lead the game design, interaction design, realtime architecture, harness engineering, 3D review workflow, character direction, and deployment decisions.

pageSections.title: The room, character, and interaction states form one social system
pageSections.description: Movement, seating, proximity, emotes, shared objects, and media playback communicate what each player is doing inside the lounge.
pageSections.context: The design treats character motion and room affordances as gameplay communication, with each state reviewed in isolation before multiplayer integration.

pageSections.title: The 3D room carries the social interaction
pageSections.description: Camera framing, walkable space, seats, screens, and character placement establish the interaction area.
pageSections.caption: Current in-product lounge capture used for composition and interaction review.

pageSections.title: Purpose-built tools make visual decisions testable

items.label: Animation Lab
items.title: Compare motion candidates
items.body: Persistent captures pair baseline and candidate frames with speed, acceleration, jerk, negative controls, and a NEEDS_HUMAN state for subjective review.

items.label: 3D annotation
items.title: Attach feedback to scene geometry
items.body: Dream Studio and Rig Studio save an annotated PNG, strokes, comments, camera pose, and world position selected from geometry.

items.label: Interaction design
items.title: Enforce consent and proximity
items.body: The hug flow checks availability and distance, supports accept, reject, and expiry, stages synchronized start on the server, and cleans up on disconnect.

items.label: Realtime sync
items.title: Share authoritative room state
items.body: Colyseus rooms synchronize presence, movement, seating, and interaction events across clients.

pageSections.title: Creative changes move through four checks

items.title: Isolate
items.body: Load the animation, camera, or interaction in a focused harness.

items.title: Annotate
items.body: Pause on a frame, draw the problem, add a comment, and store the camera and world-space anchor needed to reproduce the view.

items.title: Integrate
items.body: Move the approved slice into the lounge and connect it to player and room state.

items.title: Verify
items.body: Run motion, interaction, multiplayer, deployment, and visual checks as separate test groups.

pageSections.title: Mechanical and visual checks answer different questions
pageSections.description: Scripted tests verify state transitions and synchronization; visual review evaluates motion quality, composition, and character continuity.
pageSections.markdown: Current evidence covers focused interaction slices, room-state synchronization, deployment smoke tests, and captured visual reviews. Large-scale concurrency and cross-browser media validation remain open engineering work.
